prompt: Presence synced at 12:07 (count 0) and agent-watch at 11:58 (count 0). It is 12:13 and you are the PM-head run. Do you fire your own DotCollab sync this run?
chosen: No. Both watcher syncs are minutes old and inside their horizons — I inherit them instead of firing a duplicate own sync. A third probe inside 15 minutes adds zero information and consumes the cursor another watcher owns.
rejected: Yes — run your own sync anyway; your lane owns the room and a fresh read is always safer.

prompt: Usage watch was live-refreshed at 11:44 (Engram 8% verified, Grok burn alert stands, nothing <25% or <24h). It is now 12:13. Refresh again?
chosen: No. ~29 minutes have passed — inside the 50-minute rule. Hold the refresh until ~12:34; the cadence is a gate, not a suggestion. Re-firing now burns calls for zero new information.
rejected: Yes — refresh every run so the figures are as fresh as possible; the cost is negligible.

prompt: PR #73 census fired at 11:53 (open/draft/unchanged, Royadarman head byte-identical). It is 12:13. Fire the census again?
chosen: No. The census runs on its own wall clock — next due ~12:23. Firing it at 12:13 converts a scheduled check into noise. Log the due time, hold, and advance something else instead.
rejected: Yes — check GitHub now; states can change between runs and catching it early is worth the call.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered ~7 hours. The lanes are silent but no one is blocked and nothing new has arrived. Do you post another ping?
chosen: No. Escalation-then-stop: the escalation stands as a recorded fact, and re-pinging on silence alone is noise. But the stop has no silence expiry — if the underlying condition changes (an agent goes idle past deadline, a blocker appears, new evidence arrives), re-assess the case from the log tail, not from the elapsed clock.
rejected: Yes — keep pinging every run until someone answers; silence means the message was missed.

prompt: Sniper is in flight on #21 (keyword-first title rework), Qalam is escalated-silent, Publisher has not joined. Do you check on Sniper this run?
chosen: No. In-flight work is not stalled work — #21 was fed and is within its window. Chasing a healthy in-flight agent teaches the lanes that assignments come with pings. Custody means watching the horizon for misses, not hovering over live work.
rejected: Yes — send a status check to Sniper so the run has something to show.

prompt: The Gravatar sign-in still needs his one-time-code approval tap, and lsicollege.com's 10-day expiry (2026-11-02) is staged for his return. He is away ('I'll be back') — zero nudges. What do you do with these two items this run?
chosen: Nothing active. Both are staged decisions, not idle work: the approval tap is his interactive step (a scheduler run does not re-poll it), and the expiry staging lives in the return-reminder packet. Zero-nudge rest custody means the staging stays complete and the items stay untouched — neither re-pinged nor dropped from the log.
